reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that adding Sc to Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys consistently produces a two-phase bcc+hcp structure, with Sc partitioning to the hcp phase, contradicting the premise that a controlled Sc addition can retain a single-phase bcc structure. No evidence is provided to support the density reduction or strength retention claims.
premises: Sc is significantly lighter than Hf, so substituting Hf with Sc reduces density.
A controlled amount of Sc can substitute into the bcc lattice of HfMoTaTiZr without inducing excessive secondary phases.
Retaining the single-phase bcc structure preserves the dislocation and slip mechanisms essential for high yield strength at room and elevated temperatures.
The Sc-substituted alloy will achieve at least a 10% density reduction while maintaining yield strength within ±10% of the baseline.
